 Order

1. The petitioners are before this Court seeking for the following reliefs:
a. Call for records in Crime No.0186/2018 on the file of the Prl. Civil Judge and JMFC Court, Chintamani.
b. Quash entire proceedings in Crime No.0186/2018 on the file of the Prl. Civil Judge and JMFC Court, Chintamani registered for an offence punishable under Section 406, 409, 417, 418, 420, 482 and 506 of IPC as against these petitioners by 1st respondent police, in the interest of justice and equity.
c. Grant any other remedy deems fit in the facts and circumstance of the case.
2.
The petitioner claims to be a company registered under Companies Act, 1956 engaged in the business of manufacture and supply of E-Rickshaws and E- Carts.

3. Respondent No.2 had filed the first information with the Chintamani Town Police Station which came to be registered as crime No.186/2018 on 05.08.2018 for the offence punishable under Sections 406, 409, 417, 418, 420, 482 and 506 of IPC.
The allegation made in the first information filed by respondent NC: 2024:KHC:15095 No.2 is that the petitioner had approached the respondent No.2 for grant of dealership agreement.

The petitioner had promised to make available E- auto rickshaw passengers as also E-auto rickshaw loader i.e., for the purpose of movement of cargo, on which basis, a letter of engagement came to be issued on 04.08.2017 it being a requirement of the petitioner that two vehicles have to be bought by respondent No.2.
Respondent No.2 bought one passenger E-auto rickshaw and one loader E-auto rickshaw by making payment of the due amounts.
It is only later that respondent No.2 came to know about the petitioner not being authorized or licensed to manufacture and sell the cargo E-auto rickshaw.

When the respondent raised this issue with the petitioner, the petitioner terminated the letter of engagement/dealership agreement between the petitioner and respondent No.2 and in that background action is sought to be initiated against the petitioner for the aforesaid offences.
NC: 2024:KHC:15095 4.

The learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the entire transaction is commercial in nature inasmuch as there is a letter of agreement/dealership agreement between the petitioner and respondent No.2.
It is only on account of the dealership agreement being terminated on 04.01.2018 that first information is lodged on 05.08.2018, subsequent to the termination.
The matter being a civil dispute the alternative efficacious remedy available for the respondent is to file a civil suit and not by a criminal proceedings when the dispute is commercial in nature.

sentences.text: 3 5. Learned counsel for respondent No.2 would however submit that what has been sold to respondent No.2 on 09.10.2017 was E-rickshaw loader as also E- rickshaw passenger.
The petitioner did not have any right or authority to manufacture or sell a E-rickshaw loader.

The respondent No.2 had entered in to the arrangement with the petitioner on the basis of the NC: 2024:KHC:15095 representation which has been made by the petitioner that E-rickshaw loader or cargo vehicle could be sold at the dealership of respondent.

No such permission has been granted to the petitioner has mislead the respondent No.2 and in that background he submits that it cannot be said that the offences have not been committed by the petitioner and as such submits that the petition is required to be dismissed.

6. Having heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and respondents and having perused the documents, it is seen that the brochure which has been issued by the petitioner speaks about two vehicles.
One is E- rickshaw and other is E-cart.

E-rickshaw is stated to be a passenger vehicle and E-cart is supposed to be a cargo/goods vehicle which is known as Sweekar L.
7.

A perusal of the invoice which has been generated on 09.10.2017 indicates that the invoice has been raised in respect of E-rickshaw loader and E-rickshaw NC: 2024:KHC:15095 passenger that is to say that one of the vehicles which has been sold to respondent No.2 is a cargo vehicle.
8. Further more a perusal of the letter of engagement would indicate that all vehicles of the petitioner would be sold by respondent No.2 at the dealership.
Admittedly, the petitioner has only two vehicles.
One is the passenger and other being the cargo/goods vehicle.

The documents which have been produced do not indicate any permission granted to the petitioner permitting the petitioner to sell the goods vehicle/ cargo vehicle, nor it is registered with the RTO.
9.
That being the case, at this stage, it cannot be said that there is no offence which has been made out against the petitioner

, whether the matter is a commercial dispute, whether the petitioner is authorized to manufacture and sell a cargo E- rickshaw, whether there is RTO permission which has NC: 2024:KHC:15095 been obtained or not are all matters which are required to be established by the petitioner as a matter of defence during the course of trial.
No grounds are made out.
10. Accordingly, the petition stands dismissed.
